title: Mesh view: /hub/mesh, /hub/mesh/events (network-free)
what:
GET /hub/mesh:
- available; aoide {path, version}
- daemon {socket, ping_ms|null}: --aoide-daemon-socket receives only {"v":0,"op":"ping"}, with a 1 s timeout
- registry: nodes.json through an allowlist (name, url, verified, autogate, addedAt, grants|allows, via); pubkey, tokenFile and bearerSecret are dropped; both shapes (before and after P-CHARTER) are read
- cache: node-cache/*.json, at most 64 files of at most 64 KiB each, as text with their age
- graph: stage/graph.json, at most 2 MiB
- mesh: `mesh --json`, cached 60 s
- outbox: `mail outbox --json`, cached 60 s
- errors: sentences
GET /hub/mesh/events?after=<offset> tails --aoide-events, keeps only audit and gate classes, returns at most 64 KiB per call, and restarts at 0 when the file shrank.
Exports mesh::nodes(ctx) -> [{name, verified, meshes}] for M2. meshes comes from mesh --json, so a multi-mesh node can be offered a choice.
Never runs node list, session, send, pair, spawn, allow, node status, node pull, dispatch or anything on the A2A door.
Audit log: Aoide's own (Aoide's rule).
tests:
tests/mesh.rs:
- the fake log holds only --version, mesh --json and mail outbox --json
- no pubkey, tokenFile or bearerSecret in any response; reverting the allowlist fails this
- both registry shapes parse
- hostile cache text (HTML, script, ANSI) comes back as a JSON string
- no aoide and no state gives available:false plus a sentence
- the events tail filters classes and handles truncate-in-place
- two GETs within 60 s cause one mesh --json
- a test UnixListener sees one ping and no subscribe or dispatch
- nodes() lists meshes per node
- 401 without a token
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48108 with the fixture state.
risk: schemaVersion stayed "0" through P-CHARTER, so shape drift is invisible. X0 checks that `mail outbox --json` touches no state.
